claim: prometheus-community/smartctl_exporter requires smartmontools >= 7.0 (for JSON output), polls smartctl on a default 60s interval with a 10-minute device rescan (rescan disabled if devices are pinned via --smartctl.device or if interval < 1s), and exposes metrics on port 9633.
stance_target: Incumbent exporter cadence/privilege design that ha-linux-agent's storage collector replaces with MQTT push into HA
scope_conditions: smartctl_exporter README (585 stars, 325 commits), Go implementation
quoted_support: Requirements: smartmontools >= 7.0, because export to json released in 7.0. ... --smartctl.interval=60s The interval between smartctl polls. --smartctl.rescan=10m The interval between rescanning for new/disappeared devices.

claim: smartctl_exporter must run privileged (Docker: privileged: true, user: root) to access block devices, and maintains an explicit no-data-mutation policy: it does not fix or patch smartctl data in flight - incorrect data is reported upstream to smartmontools.
stance_target: Root/privileged requirement as a design constraint the incumbent exporter lane imposes; a NixOS agent can instead use a narrowly-scoped systemd unit with specific device permissions
scope_conditions: smartctl_exporter Docker deployment and troubleshooting policy
quoted_support: services: smartctl-exporter: image: prometheuscommunity/smartctl-exporter privileged: true user: root. ... In general, the smartctl_exporter should not modify the data in flight. If the data is missing from smartctl, it should not be in smartctl_exporter.

claim: smartctl_exporter supports systemd socket activation (--web.systemd-socket) and exporter-toolkit TLS/basic-auth via --web.config.file, showing the standard hardening surface a per-host metrics endpoint carries.
stance_target: Security surface checklist for any agent exposing host telemetry (MQTT TLS in ha-linux-agent's case)
quoted_support: --web.systemd-socket Use systemd socket activation listeners instead of port listeners (Linux only). ... --web.config.file ... [EXPERIMENTAL] Path to configuration file that can enable TLS or authentication.
